problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(2i-j)\,\text{mm}$ with a constant velocity of $(-i+j)\,\text{mm/s}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $1$ second.
worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant velocity $u,$  the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut,
$$

 
where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=2i-j,\,u=-i+j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=1\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & ={r}_{0}+ut \\  & =(2i-j)+(-i+j)(1) \\  & =(2i-j)+(-i+j) \\  & =i\,\text{mm}.\end{aligned}
$$
